raw_segments.text: Again, if the having strong and bad lusts is necessary to the idea of the man of self-control,
this character cannot be identical with the man of perfected self-mastery, because the
having strong desires, or bad ones, does not enter into the idea of this latter character.
And yet the man of self-control must have such, for suppose them good.
Then the moral state which should hinder a man from following their suggestions must
be bad, and so self-control would not be in all cases good.
Suppose them, on the other hand, to be weak and not wrong.
It would be nothing grand, nor anything great, supposing them to be wrong and weak.
